claims.claim: The method detects expressivity bottlenecks from backpropagation signals.
claims.notes: Based on description of bottleneck detection using gradient information.

claims.claim: Neurons are added to the network where the current architecture cannot follow the functional gradient.
claims.notes: Describes the growth mechanism triggered by bottleneck detection.

claims.claim: The resulting tiny networks achieve CIFAR performance matching larger models while requiring less manual architecture search.
claims.notes: Empirical result reported in the paper.

initialization_strategy: Copy weights from parent neuron with small random perturbation
mechanistic_notes: Bottleneck detection relies on misalignment between functional gradient and representable subspace of current network.
Adding neurons expands the representable subspace along the direction of the functional gradient.
selection_criterion: Expressivity bottleneck score exceeding a threshold derived from backpropagation signal magnitude
summary: The paper proposes a method that detects expressivity bottlenecks in small networks using backpropagation signals and adds neurons to alleviate them, achieving CIFAR performance comparable to larger models with reduced manual search.
website_alignment_notes: Matches the website‑aligned description of growing tiny networks that spot and fix expressivity bottlenecks optimally.
